components: a longer lower stroke that curves down on the left and runs out to the right
strokeOrder: draw the short upper stroke from left to right
lift, begin at the left and curve down, then run out to the right along the base, rising slightly at the end
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 03053 file records こ as two stroke paths in this order and direction: the upper stroke, then the lower curve; so there is one pen lift.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/03053.svg, hiragana こ (U+3053 HIRAGANA LETTER KO), two stroke paths kvg:03053-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the upper stroke drawn left to right, ending in a small turn down and back to the left that the print glyph does not show; s2 starts at the left, curves down and runs out to the right along the base, rising slightly at its end. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs.

notes: Opens こんにちは; shares an ancestor with katakana コ.
